items.abstract: The brick industry is one of the informal sectors vulnerable to the risk of occupational diseases due to exposure to dust, combustion fumes, and direct contact with soil. Knowledge, attitudes, and compliance with the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) play an important role in preventing health complaints among workers. This study aims to analyze the relationship between knowledge, attitudes, and compliance with the use of PPE and complaints of occupational diseases among brick industry workers in Neuheun Village, Aceh Besar. This study used a quantitative observational analytic method with a cross-sectional approach. The sample consisted of 65 respondents selected using the total sampling technique and analyzed using the Chi-Square test. The results showed that 52.3% of respondents had good knowledge, 53.8% had poor attitudes, and 66.2% did not comply with PPE use. A total of 55.4% of respondents experienced occupational health complaints. The statistical analysis showed no significant relationship between knowledge and occupational health complaints (p = 0.056), whereas attitude (p = 0.021) and compliance (p < 0.001) were significantly associated with occupational health complaints. It can be concluded that good knowledge needs to be accompanied by positive attitudes and greater compliance with PPE use to support the prevention of occupational health problems.

items.title: Human Factor Contributions to Accidents and Fatalities in U.S. Construction: A Comparative Analysis of Three Major Subsectors
items.abstract: Human factors remain a leading cause of occupational accidents and fatalities in the construction industry. Although human factors are a major contributor to construction accidents, their relative impact across different construction subsectors has not been fully quantified. This study presents a comparative analysis of accident and fatality data from the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) for three major construction subsectors, NAICS 236 (Construction of Buildings), 237 (Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction), and 238 (Specialty Trade Contractors) from January 2010 through June 2025. Seventy human-factor-related keywords were categorized into eight categories, and accident counts, fatality counts, and fatality rates, defined as the proportion of investigated cases that were fatal, were computed. Twenty-four high-frequency keywords (≥60 investigated accidents) were further analyzed across the three subsectors. Descriptive methods, including risk matrices, Pareto analysis, and category-level fatality rate comparisons, were applied to identify the factors contributing most to fatalities. Differences between subsectors were tested using permutation-based chi-square tests with Benjamini–Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons. Results indicate substantial variation in both frequency and severity among keywords. items.title: Human-Centered AI in Practice: Peer Facilitators as Technostress Reducers in a Mixed-Methods LMS Study
items.abstract: Purpose: While the rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) offers significant pedagogical potential, it often outpaces the psychological scaffolding that anxious learners require, creating a severe affective barrier known as technostress. To address this critical gap, this study investigates whether structured peer facilitation, embedded within a Learning Management System (LMS) based AI course, can effectively reduce undergraduate students' AI anxiety and strengthen their conceptual understanding. Methods/Study design/approach: An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was conducted involving 33 undergraduate students encountering generative AI instruction for the first time. Quantitative data encompassing AI anxiety, conceptual understanding, an)d technical self-efficacy were collected pre- and post-intervention, followed by analysis using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Spearman's rank correlation. Subsequently, qualitative data from open-ended evaluations were examined through reflexive thematic analysis to contextualize and deeply explain the quantitative shifts. Result/Findings: The intervention yielded a statistically significant reduction in AI anxiety (Z = -2.151, p = .032) alongside a significant improvement in conceptual understanding (Z = -1.990, p = .047). Although technical self-efficacy and career projection improved, the changes did not reach statistical significance. Furthermore, facilitator evaluation exhibited a significant negative correlation with anxiety reduction (rs = -.389). Thematic analysis confirmed that peer facilitators effectively acted as technical translators and technostress reducers, establishing the psychological safety necessary for learning. Novelty/Originality/Value: This research uniquely repositions peer mediation as the vital affective "more capable other" within Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development, prioritizing the resolution of emotional barriers before cognitive engagement with AI tools. The study extends Human-Centered AI (HCAI) theory by delivering robust empirical evidence that pairing generative AI modules with human peer facilitation creates a synergistic learning ecosystem. This provides educators with a scalable, practical solution for mitigating technostress in modern digital education.

items.title: Human-Centred AI for Sustainable Digital Governance in India: A Review of Digital Public Services.
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to improve public service delivery through automation, data analysis, decision support and digital interaction. In India, Digital India, Digital Public Infrastructure and national AI initiatives have created opportunities to make government services more efficient, accessible and responsive. At the same time, AI-enabled public services raise concerns related to privacy, transparency, bias, accessibility, accountability and citizen trust. This paper examines how a Human-Centred AI (HCAI) approach can support sustainable digital governance in India through a structured review of secondary literature. Recent peer-reviewed studies, government reports and institutional publications are examined using thematic analysis. The review focuses on citizen-centric service delivery, accessibility and inclusion, transparency and explainability, privacy and security, fairness, citizen trust, and human oversight. The findings indicate that AI can support intelligent service discovery, conversational assistance, multilingual interaction, personalisation and routine administrative processing. However, technological capability alone does not guarantee better public services. AI must be designed around citizen needs and supported by appropriate governance safeguards. Based on the synthesis, the paper proposes a conceptual Human-Centred AI Framework with five interconnected dimensions: human needs, inclusive digital experience, responsible AI, accountable governance and sustainable public value. The paper concludes that India's AI-enabled digital governance should balance technological innovation with accessibility, privacy, fairness, transparency, human oversight and public trust.

items.title: Human-Centred Psychological Support in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Prospects for Employee Well-Being and Organizational Trust
items.abstract: Psychological support in corporations has traditionally relied on interpersonal mechanisms, including manager support, employee assistance programmes, counselling, stress-management interventions, and occupational health services. The diffusion of artificial intelligence is changing not only the instruments used to support employees, but also the psychological architecture of support itself. This study examines how corporate psychological support has evolved from predominantly human-centred models to hybrid systems that incorporate artificial intelligence, with particular attention to psychological safety, trust, autonomy, perceived organizational support, emotional disclosure, stress, burnout, and surveillance-related anxiety. An integrative conceptual review and comparative synthesis were conducted using established theories of occupational psychology and recent evidence on workplace mental health, digital mental-health interventions, conversational agents, technostress, and AI-enabled management. The analysis applies the Job Demands-Resources model, psychological safety theory, and perceived organizational support as complementary explanatory lenses. The study identifies a transition from reactive and episodic support toward preventive, continuous, and increasingly personalized support. AI can strengthen psychological resources by improving accessibility, low-threshold help-seeking, personalization, and early identification of distress. However, the same technologies can become psychological demands when employees experience monitoring as surveillance, data collection as loss of privacy, automated recommendations as reduced autonomy, or simulated empathy as depersonalized care. AI does not inherently improve or deteriorate employee well-being. Its psychological effect depends on whether it is embedded in a human-centred support system that preserves confidentiality, voluntary participation, meaningful human contact, and professional accountability. Future studies should test the proposed dual-path model across occupations and cultures and examine how human oversight, perceived organizational motives, and AI literacy moderate the relationship between AI-mediated support and employee psychological outcomes.

items.title: Human-inspired Route Selection for Efficient Social Robot Navigation in Narrow Spaces
items.abstract: Narrow human environments are challenging for social robot navigation, where distance-optimal shortcut routes to destination are frequently blocked by people in the aisles. People in these situations select the appropriate route between detour and shortcut in an efficient and socially-aware way, by balancing their extra effort (if choosing detour) and the required effort from the person on the way to make space to pass. Similar balance strategy is utilized when people decide the politeness of the request utterance to compensate for the way yielding effort from others. Inspired by this human balance strategy, we developed a decision-making methodological framework for socially-aware high-level path planning and interaction utterance when the robot navigates in narrow shared spaces and implemented it onto a humanoid mobile robot. In order to demonstrate the transparency and utility of this framework, we present a specific instantiation by conducting a set of human-robot experiments in a real store. Data from 30 people were collected via two field experiments to identify socially-acceptable parameters. Results of a within-participants study with 28 human customers interestingly demonstrated that the proposed socially-aware method was more time-efficient compared to the detour-only and shortcut-only strategies.

items.title: Human-Routed Handoffs in ChatGPT: A Possibly More Token-Efficient Procedure for Cross-Surface Work
items.abstract: This paper proposes a human-routed procedure for maintaining continuity across ChatGPT conversations and work surfaces.Derived from developing papers and a screenplay, it separates two objects: a Dump preserves relevant discussion; a Handoff directs the next operation. Verbatim and Summary Dumps offer different levels of fidelity and compression.Two controls govern the procedure: Authority Space bounds jurisdiction; Goodwill bounds optimization after sufficiency. Handoffs must remain checkable, with review proportionate to consequences and the object’s validity conditions.The procedure may reduce reconstruction and token use while preserving human judgment and responsibility. These benefits are practical observations rather than quantified or universal claims. The proposal is offered for adaptation, testing, correction, or rejection.

items.title: Hybrid feature selection with SHAP-based explainable AI for interpretable phishing website detection
items.abstract: Phishing websites remain a significant cybersecurity threat, exploiting users through deceptive web interfaces and continuously evolving attack strategies. Despite the effectiveness of machine learning approaches, many existing solutions suffer from limited interpretability, redundant feature representations, and evaluation practices that may lead to overly optimistic performance estimates. This study proposes a phishing website detection framework that integrates hybrid feature selection with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). The proposed approach combines Mutual Information, Χ², and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based feature importance to identify the most informative and discriminative features from complementary statistical, information-theoretic, and model-driven perspectives. The framework was evaluated using the PhiUSIIL dataset and further validated on an external URL-only dataset to assess generalization capability. To ensure reliable performance estimation and prevent information leakage, feature selection was performed independently within each fold of a 10-fold stratified cross-validation procedure. Five machine learning classifiers, namely Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, were evaluated using classifier-specific feature subsets generated independently within the cross-validation procedure. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid feature selection framework substantially reduces the feature space while maintaining predictive performance comparable to that achieved using all available features. Across the evaluated classifiers, XGBoost provided the most balanced overall performance. Additional analyses showed that the near-perfect performance observed on the PhiUSIIL dataset was dataset-dependent, with lower performance obtained on the external dataset and under an oracle-informed worst-case feature perturbation scenario, highlighting the sensitivity of the framework under more demanding evaluation conditions. SHAP further improves model interpretability by providing both global and local explanations of feature contributions while supporting the feature selection process. Overall, the findings demonstrate that integrating statistical, information-theoretic, and explainability-driven feature selection can substantially reduce feature dimensionality while preserving predictive performance and improving model interpretability. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and computationally efficient basis for phishing website detection, while its practical deployment remains dependent on feature-extraction costs and validation under heterogeneous operational conditions.

items.title: Hyper-Personalization vs. Privacy Paradox: Balancing AI-Driven Customer Insights with Consumer Data Ethics and Trust
items.abstract: Abstract: The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence and machine learning has enabled organizations to achieve unprecedented levels of hyper-personalization, transforming how brands interact with consumers. However, this capability intensifies the privacy paradox, a phenomenon where consumers express profound concern for data privacy while simultaneously trading personal information for tailored experiences and immediate utility. This paper examines the complex equilibrium required to harness AI-driven customer insights without eroding consumer data ethics and organizational trust. Traditional data collection frameworks are increasingly inadequate in managing the granular, predictive datasets utilized by modern personalization algorithms. As predictive analytics decipher behavioral patterns, purchasing intent, and real-time location data, the ethical threshold for consent, transparency, and data minimization rises significantly. Organizations frequently struggle to balance the commercial imperatives of hyper-targeted engagement with regulatory compliance, such as the General Data Protection Regulation and evolving global privacy standards. This research investigates how opaque data practices and aggressive profiling lead to algorithmic fatigue, consumer alienation, and catastrophic trust erosion. The study analyzes the mechanics of transparent data stewardship, exploring how organizations can implement ethical AI frameworks that prioritize consumer agency, explicit consent architecture, and explainable algorithmic models. By adopting privacy-by-design principles and federated learning techniques, businesses can derive deep consumer insights without compromising individual anonymity or data security. Furthermore, the paper highlights the strategic advantage of ethical positioning, demonstrating that transparent data practices transform compliance from a legal burden into a distinct market differentiator. Methodologically, this study combines a comprehensive review of contemporary digital ethics literature with empirical case analyses of firms navigating data breaches versus those successfully cultivating trust-based personalization ecosystems. The findings reveal that sustainable customer lifetime value is directly correlated with perceived data fairness and control. Ultimately, the paper provides a strategic roadmap for leaders to align AI-driven marketing capabilities with robust ethical safeguards, ensuring that hyper-personalization fosters long-term brand loyalty rather than opportunistic exploitation.

items.title: Identity-Bound Governance Under Execution Uncertainty: An Accountability Proof Block for LLM Agent Persistent Halts, with Cryptographic Implementation and Cross-Model Calibration
items.abstract: A correctly governed LLM agent can reach a state in which neither continuing execution nor automatically halting is admissible: the system has detected a persistent failure of its observability or drift-detection layer, but cannot itself decide who has the authority to resume, deny, or recalibrate the deployment. We call this an identity-bound governance event and formalise the mechanism that resolves it. We introduce the Accountability Proof Block (APB): a system-constructed evidence block, a human-supplied decision block, and an ed25519 signature binding both to a registered principal. The system cannot forge the signature, and the principal cannot alter the evidence undetected. We prove four theorems: Protocol-Bounded Governance Completeness, Non-Repudiability, Impossibility of Anonymous Re-Authorization, and Finite-Time APB Construction Termination. The implementation uses RFC 8785 JSON canonicalization and a UUID4-based replay predicate. Empirically, governance completeness holds over 3,812 halt events with zero unresolved cases; the verifier detects 100% of 1,800 attacks across 9 adversarial vectors; a k-of-n multi-principal variant shows 0 false acceptances in 2,000 single-key capture attempts. A study of six open LLMs finds the drift threshold T* stable within model (sigma/T* < 2%) but varying across models, refuting size-monotonicity: the largest model did not drift. T* must therefore be measured per deployment, and the APB is the vehicle by which that threshold yields accountable authority transfer.

items.abstract: This repository contains supplementary materials for the paper "AI-Assisted Generation of Bloom's-Aligned Assessments: A Comparative Study of Prompting Strategies and Assessment Quality," accepted at IEEE TALE 2026. The study investigated an AI-assisted pipeline using GPT-5.2 (via Perplexity Pro) to generate multiple-choice and short-answer questions aligned to Bloom's Taxonomy for a biomedical engineering module (BN2201, Quantitative Physiology for Bioengineers). Few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting strategies were compared via educator evaluation (RQ1), and AI-generated items were subsequently compared against human-authored items in an authentic midterm examination (RQ2). Materials are organized into two components: Generation Metadata, Prompts & Analysis Code (public): LLM configuration, prompt templates, and R code for inter-rater reliability analysis. Item Pool and Examination Materials (restricted access): Instructor-provided exemplars, the AI-generated item pool, and examination design. Access to this component is restricted to preserve item integrity for future use in the module; researchers may contact the corresponding author for access. items.title: Image Classifiers are Efficient Self-Supervised Video Representation Learners
items.abstract: We introduce VideoMSN, a Masked Siamese Network framework for efficient self-supervised spatio-temporal representation learning in videos. Instead of relying on heavy 3D architectures or reconstruction-based autoencoders for learning with unlabeled data, we repurpose standard image Vision Transformers by representing videos as super images which are grids composed of frames sampled from videos. From each super image, we construct two views: one with spatial patch masking and the other with temporal frame masking, ensuring no information leakage across frames. A shared Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder aligns their embeddings using a masked Siamese loss, capturing both motion and appearance cues without reconstruction. Our decoder-free formulation leverages an image foundation model towards efficient video representation learning. Starting from pretrained DINO-v3 and DeiT-v3 image encoders, VideoMSN achieves state-of-the-art performance on Kinetics-400, UCF101, and HMDB51 while requiring up to $32\times$ fewer and $160\times$ fewer video pretraining epochs compared to prior video self-supervised learning methods. Our proposed approach also shows strong performance in low-shot classification, confirming the transferability of the learned representations in a label-scarce scenario. items.title: IMoKGNN: Dual-Stream Fusion of Generic and Task-Specific Language Model Features for Graph Neural Networks
items.abstract: Text-Attributed Graphs (TAGs) are prevalent in various real-world scenarios, where each node is associated with a text attribute. Representation learning on TAGs relies on a comprehensive understanding of both the textual attributes and the topological connections. Recent works have enhanced graph neural networks (GNNs) with pre-trained language models (PLMs) for textual attribute modeling, achieving promising results compared with shallow text representations such as BoW. With the advent of more powerful LLMs, how to effectively and efficiently inject the generic knowledge in LLMs into representation learning on TAGs still calls for systematic investigation. To this end, we first examine whether mainstream generative LLMs can provide high-quality generic text embeddings that can be directly used by downstream GNNs, and further explore their complementarity with the task-specific knowledge from a tuned PLM (TLM). Based on these observations, we propose a dual-channel knowledge fusion framework, named MoKGNN, to simultaneously leverage the generic semantic knowledge from LLMs and the task adaptation capability of TLM. Specifically, we design a dual-channel feature extraction module to learn generic and task-specific text representations separately. Next, we introduce a Knowledge Alignment Network to align the LLM embeddings with the TLM representations. Finally, MoKGNN adopts a global mixing weight to fuse the two channels, obtaining a unified node embedding for downstream GNN training. Moreover, we further analyze a key limitation of such early feature fusion under message passing: once heterogeneous text features are merged before neighborhood aggregation, source-specific noise and non-aligned semantics may be diffused together and become harder to disentangle and correct. Motivated by this observation, we propose IMoKGNN, a decoupled dual-stream framework that propagates LLM and TLM features in parallel with a shared GNN backbone and performs late fusion in logit space. Extensive experiments on five TAG datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approaches for both node classification and link prediction, and show that IMoKGNN yields more reliable improvements than MoKGNN.

items.title: Impact of AI-Enabled Features in Faculty Teaching Effectiveness in Google Classroom
items.abstract: Abstract The Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration into education is transforming traditional teaching and learning practices. Google Classroom, currently with AI-enabled features such as lesson-plan generation, quiz creation, rubric development, differentiated learning resources, and suggested feedback, provides faculty with special power to improve teaching efficiency and classroom management. This study examines the impact of AI-enabled features on faculty teaching effectiveness in Google Classroom. The study mainly focuses on how AI influences lesson planning, preparation time, assessment, feedback, personalization of learning, student engagement, and overall teaching effectiveness. The study can be conducted using a structured questionnaire among faculty members who use Google Classroom. The findings are expected to show that AI can reduce routine workload and support more efficient and personalized teaching. However, factors such as AI literacy, training, accuracy of AI-generated content, privacy concerns, and the need for human supervision may influence its effectiveness. Research on AI in education also emphasizes the importance of teacher professional development and responsible implementation.

items.title: Impact Of Artificial Intelligence-Based Fitness Applications On Physical Activity Participation And Health Behaviour Among Undergraduate Students In Federal Universities In North-West Nigeria
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI) based fitness applications on physical activity participation and health behaviour among the undergraduates of Federal Universities, North-West Nigeria. The four objectives, four research questions, and four null hypotheses were the compass of this study. For the study, a descriptive correlational survey research design was used. The population consisted of undergraduate students of a few Federal Universities in the Northwest Nigeria. 384 undergraduate students were chosen as respondents using a multistage sampling technique. The Artificial Intelligence Fitness Applications, Physical Activity and Health Behaviour Questionnaire (AIFAPHBQ) was used to gather data. The internal consistency of the instrument was evaluated by Cronbach's Alpha reliability technique and the overall reliability coefficient obtained was 0.84. It was endorsed by experts in the field of Physical and Health Education, Educational Technology, and Measurement and Evaluation. The mean and the standard deviation were used to solve the problems in the study, while the independent-samples t-test and Pearson Product Moment Correlation were applied to test the null hypotheses at 0.05 level of significance. Based on the results, the use of AI-based fitness apps among undergraduate students was at moderate level (Grand Mean = 2.84, SD = 0.76). Use of the AI fitness app was positively associated with physical activity participation (r = .61, p < .001) and health behaviour (r = .58, p < .001). The results also revealed that male students felt they were using AI based fitness apps slightly more than female students, but this was not statistically significant (t = 1.63, p = .104). The researchers found that there is significant potential for the use of AI fitness apps to boost physical activity participation and promote positive health behaviours among undergraduate students. It suggests that digital health education, implementing institutional wellness programmes, and enhancing access to relevant digital infrastructure should be encouraged to promote responsible and health-oriented use of AI-based fitness technologies at universities.

items.title: Impact of Generative AI on Formal Writing Skills of Undergraduate students
items.abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has significantly influenced students' approach to formal writing. The present research, titled “Impact of Generative AI on the Formal Writing Practices of Undergraduate Students,” tries to examine the extent, frequency, purposes, and perceived effects of Generative AI used by undergraduate students in formal writing. A descriptive survey research design along with a quantitative approach was applied. A structured online questionnaire was prepared using Google Forms to collect primary data from undergraduate students representing programmes such as B.A., BMS, BAF, B.Com., B.Sc. Computer Science, B.Sc. IT, Psychology, History, and B.A.M.M.C. A total of 108 responses were obtained. Non-probability convenience sampling was used, and responses were analysed on the basis of frequency and percentage analysis, along with interpretation of Likert-scale responses. The findings show that a considerable number of undergraduate students use Generative AI in formal writing practices, which is clear as 94 out of 108 respondents (86.9%) selecting previous use of Generative AI for formal writing. ChatGPT proved to be the most popular Generative AI tool used by the students, followed by Google Gemini and Claude. The study reveals students’ use of AI for generating ideas, drafting content, improving grammar and language, summarising information, and editing written work. This study is aimed at finding out the degree of AI help in formal writing, the level of students' improvement in their writing skills, confidence in writing without AI help, acceptance of AI-written content without major editing, and their readiness to keep using the tools. This study reveals the significance of Generative AI in the field of formal writing of undergraduates and the advantages, as well as possible drawbacks, connected to their dependence on the technology. These results can be helpful in studying the influence of Generative AI on the writing process of students and will help the educational institutions and teachers to encourage proper and ethical use of Generative AI by students.

items.title: Impact of Learning Environment on Students' Achievement
items.abstract: This study aimed to determine the influence of the learning environment on students’ achievement at Southern de Oro Philippines College, focusing specifically on peer influence, teacher approachability, and the availability of learning resources. The research adopted a correlational and causal design supplemented by documentary analysis. Data were gathered from 238 students across BSIT, CBAE, and CHTM programs during the 2025–2026 school year using a modified, validated questionnaire. Analysis involved descriptive statistics, correlation, and multiple linear regression to evaluate relationships and predictive effects. Findings revealed that the learning environment was generally rated high, with peer influence particularly strong, alongside favorable levels of teacher approachability and learning resources availability. Students’ achievement was also assessed at a satisfactory to good level. However, peer influence, teacher approachability, and learning resources availability showed no significant correlation or predictive influence on achievement. The study concludes that, despite a positive learning environment, these specific factors do not directly influence on students’ academic outcomes. Other variables, such as intrinsic motivation or external support systems, likely exert greater influence. Recommendations include peer mentoring initiatives and enhanced teacher training for better student engagement.

items.title: Importance Of Science In National Development: Building The Foundation Of Viksit Bharat @2047
items.abstract: Abstract: Science has emerged as one of the most influential forces shaping economic growth, social transformation and national progress in the twenty-first century. The development of modern societies is increasingly dependent on the ability to create scientific knowledge, translate that knowledge into technological innovations and ensure that these innovations reach different sections of society. For a country such as India, which is simultaneously addressing issues of economic development, population growth, employment, education, healthcare, agriculture, energy security and environmental sustainability, science has a particularly important role to play. Scientific advancement can provide evidence-based and innovative solutions to complex national challenges while also strengthening India's competitiveness in the global knowledge economy. The vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 represents India's aspiration to become a developed nation by the centenary of independence. This vision encompasses not merely higher economic growth but also improvements in human development, education, healthcare, infrastructure, employment, social equity, technological capability, environmental sustainability and quality of life. Science and technology can serve as connecting forces among these different dimensions of development. Advances in agricultural science can improve productivity and climate resilience; medical science can support affordable healthcare; digital technologies can improve access to public services and education; space science can support communication, navigation and disaster management; renewable-energy research can strengthen energy security; and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, robotics and quantum technologies can create new opportunities for innovation and economic growth. The present paper examines the multidimensional importance of science in India's development with particular reference to Viksit Bharat @2047. It adopts a descriptive and analytical approach based on secondary information obtained from policy documents, government reports, scientific institutions, educational literature and international development reports. The paper discusses the contribution of science to economic development, agriculture, healthcare, education, industry, digital transformation, space technology, renewable energy and environmental sustainability. It further explores the role of scientific education in developing curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving ability and innovation among young people. The paper also identifies significant challenges, including unequal access to scientific resources, the digital divide, inadequate research infrastructure in some areas, limited industry-academia collaboration, shortage of specialised human resources, brain drain and the gap between scientific research and its practical application. The paper argues that the achievement of Viksit Bharat @2047 requires a transition from a technology-consuming society to a knowledge-generating and innovation-driven society. The vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 represents India's aspiration to become a developed nation by the centenary of independence. This vision encompasses not merely higher economic growth but also improvements in human development, education, healthcare, infrastructure, employment, social equity, technological capability, environmental sustainability and quality of life. Science and technology can serve as connecting forces among these different dimensions of development. Advances in agricultural science can improve productivity and climate resilience; medical science can support affordable healthcare; digital technologies can improve access to public services and education; space science can support communication, navigation and disaster management; renewable-energy research can strengthen energy security; and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, robotics and quantum technologies can create new opportunities for innovation and economic growth. The present paper examines the multidimensional importance of science in India's development with particular reference to Viksit Bharat @2047. It adopts a descriptive and analytical approach based on secondary information obtained from policy documents, government reports, scientific institutions, educational literature and international development reports. The paper discusses the contribution of science to economic development, agriculture, healthcare, education, industry, digital transformation, space technology, renewable energy and environmental sustainability. It further explores the role of scientific education in developing curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving ability and innovation among young people. The paper also identifies significant challenges, including unequal access to scientific resources, the digital divide, inadequate research infrastructure in some areas, limited industry-academia collaboration, shortage of specialised human resources, brain drain and the gap between scientific research and its practical application. The paper argues that the achievement of Viksit Bharat @2047 requires a transition from a technology-consuming society to a knowledge-generating and innovation-driven society. items.title: IMPROVING THE METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK FOR FUNCTIONAL ASSESSMENT OF HUMANITARIAN DEMINING SPECIALIST PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT KITS
items.abstract: The article presents an improved methodological framework for the functional assessment of personal protective equipment (PPE) intended for humanitarian demining specialists. The relevance of the study is determined by the growing need for standardized and reproducible procedures for evaluating the ergonomic suitability, operational effectiveness, and functional compatibility of protective equipment used during mine action operations. Humanitarian demining activities are associated with increased physical, limited visibility, restricted mobility, and high operational risks; therefore, PPE must provide not only ballistic and fragmentation protection but also sufficient functionality for safe execution of demining tasks. The study analyzes the current Ukrainian regulatory and legal framework governing mine action activities and compares it with relevant international standards and technical recommendations. The conducted analysis demonstrates that existing Ukrainian legislation regulates organizational, managerial, and certification aspects of mine action but does not establish a dedicated methodology for evaluating the ergonomic and functional suitability of deminer PPE. This creates significant difficulties in conducting objective comparative testing and in making evidence-based decisions regarding operational applicability of protective equipment. The purpose of the research is to improve the methodological apparatus for functional evaluation of humanitarian demining PPE considering the requirements of Ukrainian legislation and international standards. The research methodology includes comparative regulatory analysis, classification of PPE systems, development of functional assessment procedures, and formalization of result interpretation algorithms. The proposed framework is based on the principles of functional representativeness, repeatability, traceability, and practical applicability of testing results. PPE systems are classified into light and heavy categories depending on their protective structure, mobility restrictions, and operational characteristics. The methodology introduces a structured matrix of functional tests, including emergency quick-release assessment, visor visibility evaluation, finger dexterity testing, manipulation with probing tools, mobility assessment, posture transition evaluation, and control of dangerous gaps between protective elements during movement. Particular attention is devoted to defining scoring criteria, minimum admissible thresholds, participant selection requirements, and averaging algorithms for individual and group assessment results. Mandatory and additional tests are differentiated according to PPE category and operational conditions. The methodology also establishes formalized rules for determining whether a PPE configuration satisfies functional suitability requirements. The practical applicability of the proposed approach is demonstrated through comparative assessment of two PPE configurations differing in torso protection design. The obtained results confirm that the methodology allows objective comparison of protective systems, improves reproducibility of testing procedures, and supports evidencebased selection of PPE for humanitarian demining operations. The developed methodological apparatus may be applied during certification procedures, procurement activities, comparative field trials, and further mathematical modeling of integrated PPE suitability indicators.

items.title: Increasing Width Allows Greedy Layer-wise Training to Rival End-to-End Backpropagation in Self-Supervised Learning
items.abstract: End-to-end backpropagation has been the dominant mode of training in deep learning, allowing for the coordination of parameter updates across layers of a neural network. Prior studies have explored alternative -- and, in some cases, simpler -- training mechanisms, showing that they can sometimes achieve performance similar to backpropagation. However, the architectural conditions under which locally optimized networks, which avoid end-to-end backpropagation of error, can learn representations comparable to those learned through end-to-end training remain unclear. We aim to answer this question in the context of self-supervised learning, an important framework for large-scale pretraining in artificial intelligence. Here, we investigate how network width and depth affect the efficacy of greedy layer-wise and end-to-end self-supervised training in convolutional networks. We find that in wider networks, the benefits of end-to-end backpropagation over greedy layer-wise training shrink: in relatively shallow and very wide networks, we even observed higher performance in models trained with greedy layer-wise training. Subsequent analysis of the representations formed by these networks shows that very wide greedy-trained networks exhibit more favorable representational geometry than do networks trained end-to-end with backpropagation. This work shows that width can compensate for restricted credit assignment and identifies differences in representational geometry as a potential mechanism for their improved performance.

items.title: Indirect associations involving four work-motivation dimensions between perceived organizational climate and work engagement among geriatric nursing assistants in China: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Population ageing has increased demand for long-term care, yet evidence on organizational and motivational correlates of work engagement among geriatric nursing assistants in China remains limited. Using convenience sampling, this cross-sectional survey recruited geriatric nursing assistants from nine aged care institutions in Xi’an and Weinan, Shaanxi Province, China, between May and August 2025. Of 396 returned questionnaires, 330 were included after prespecified data screening. Participants completed measures of perceived organizational climate, four work-motivation dimensions, and work engagement. Pearson correlations, observed-score regressions, four separate structural equation models, and 5,000-resample bias-corrected bootstrap analyses were conducted. Institution- and covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses were also performed. In the joint regression model, intrinsic motivation ( β = 0.420, p < 0.001) and introjected regulation ( β = 0.324, p < 0.001) were independently associated with work engagement, whereas perceived organizational climate, identified regulation, and external regulation were not. Across the four structural equation models, perceived organizational climate was positively associated with each motivation dimension (standardized β = 0.652–0.704), and each motivation dimension was positively associated with work engagement ( β = 0.543–0.771). Because each model included only one motivation dimension, the indirect estimates were model-specific rather than unique contributions independent of the other dimensions. Significant indirect associations were observed through intrinsic motivation ( β = 0.519, bias-corrected 95% CI [0.430, 0.636]), identified regulation ( β = 0.430, [0.349, 0.532]), introjected regulation ( β = 0.530, [0.439, 0.648]), and external regulation ( β = 0.359, [0.258, 0.497]). In separate sensitivity analyses based on standardized observed scores, the four indirect associations remained statistically significant after adjustment for institutions and selected individual-level covariates. Perceived organizational climate and the four work-motivation dimensions were associated with work engagement among geriatric nursing assistants. The findings support further investigation of how organizational conditions and qualitatively different forms of work motivation relate to engagement. Because all variables were measured concurrently, temporal ordering and causal mediation cannot be established.

items.title: Inference Auctions
items.abstract: When inference demand exceeds available compute capacity, model providers must decide which requests should be served first. Users have different tolerances for delay from an LLM API, but current priority pricing schemes compress these differences into coarse fixed-price service tiers. We design an inference auction that allows users to bid for faster service. Our auction allocates priority in an economically efficient way without sacrificing latency, and we develop fast algorithms for implementing prices that incentivize truthful bidding. We also design an autobidding agent for our inference auction, where users specify an inference budget and the autobidder dynamically adjusts its bids over time to maximize user utility subject to the budget constraint. Experiments validate the practicality of our auction: it increases system welfare while maintaining the cache utilization and latency advantages of SGLang, a state-of-the-art inference serving framework.

items.abstract: The study analyzes the potential of generative AI technologies to address students' individual learning needs, differentiate instructional materials, develop English language skills (lexical, grammatical, communicative, and receptive-productive), provide immediate feedback, and support independent learning. The methodological framework of the study comprises systemic, comparative, linguo-didactic, and modeling methods. The results indicate that generative AI tools create additional opportunities for transitioning from a "one-size-fits-all" assignment approach to an individualized and differentiated teaching model in inclusive English language education. At the same time, issues such as the accuracy of AI-generated content, academic integrity, data privacy, the risk of excessive student reliance on AI, and the maintenance of teacher oversight were identified as critical methodological considerations.

items.title: INNOVATIVE APPROACHES TO DEVELOPING STUDENTS' FOREIGN LANGUAGE COMMUNICATIVE COMPETENCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of foreign language communicative competence has become an essential component of contemporary higher education. The increasing internationalization of academic and professional environments requires university students to use foreign languages not only for understanding linguistic information but also for participating effectively in academic discussions, professional communication, intercultural interaction, collaborative projects, and digital communication. This article examines innovative approaches to developing students’ foreign language communicative competence in higher education. Particular attention is given to communicative, task-based, project-based, learner-centered, collaborative, and technology-enhanced approaches. The study analyzes the relationship between linguistic knowledge and practical communicative performance and identifies pedagogical conditions that contribute to students’ active participation in foreign language learning. The role of authentic materials, professional contexts, digital platforms, artificial intelligence, peer interaction, reflective learning, and formative assessment is also considered. The article proposes an integrated pedagogical framework in which foreign language instruction is organized around meaningful communicative tasks, learner autonomy, professional relevance, and continuous feedback. The proposed approach is intended to facilitate students’ transition from controlled language practice to independent and context-sensitive communication. Keywords: foreign language education, communicative competence, university students, innovative approaches, task-based learning, project-based learning, digital technologies, learner autonomy, intercultural communication, formative assessment.

items.title: Integrated approaches to food and beverage safety: assessing contaminants, nutritional quality and emerging detection technologies for public health enhancement
items.abstract: This review synthesises integrated strategies for safeguarding food and beverage safety, with emphasis on emerging contaminants, nutritional quality, and public health implications. Key contaminants, particularly microplastics (MPs) and synthetic dyes, are increasingly detected in packaged foods, bottled water, salt, and beverages, raising significant safety concerns. Recent studies reported a wide variability in MPs contamination across regions and food types, reflecting the absence of standardised detection protocols. Advances in analytical technologies, including nanomaterial-based electrochemical sensors, green microextraction techniques, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted detection platforms, have improved sensitivity and selectivity, although further validation and industrial scalability remain necessary. Similarly, research on synthetic dyes highlights progress in sustainable extraction and detection methods, such as deep eutectic solvent (DES) microextraction and sensor innovation, aligning with the growing shift toward eco-efficient analytical practices. This review also evaluates the nutritional and metabolic impacts of ultra-processed foods (UPFs), which represent a major component of modern diets and are consistently associated with obesity, metabolic syndrome, and other non-communicable diseases. Cross-country analyses revealed excessive sugar, salt, and fat content in UPFs, alongside gaps in front-of-package labelling systems and limited consumer literacy. These findings underscore the need for harmonised nutritional profiling frameworks and product reformulation policies. In addition, the role of probiotics in enhancing microbial safety and functional beverage quality is examined. Emerging microencapsulation techniques show promise in improving probiotic survival and bioactivity during storage and digestion, though mechanistic insights remain limited. Policy assessments indicate that fiscal measures, advertising regulations, and labelling requirements are inconsistently applied across nations, revealing persistent misalignment between technological innovations, regulatory implementation, and consumer behaviour. Three major research gaps are identified: (i) the lack of standardised, validated analytical methods for emerging contaminants; (ii) limited mechanistic understanding of probiotic stability and functionality in beverage systems; and (iii) insufficient integration of culturally adaptive, consumer-centred policy strategies. Future research should prioritise harmonised analytical frameworks, scalable and sustainable detection technologies, a clearer understanding of probiotic mechanisms, and comprehensive nutritional databases. Strong multisectoral collaboration among scientists, industry, and policymakers is crucial to translate these advances into effective public health actions. Collectively, this review highlights the need for an integrated, multidisciplinary approach that unites technological innovation, nutritional science, and evidence-based regulation to ensure the safety of food and beverages worldwide.

The study uses a qualitative, conceptual and document-based design based on verified official and authoritative sources. India’s composite SDG Index score rose from 57 in 2018 to 71 in 2023–24; Maharashtra’s composite score in 2023–24 was 69. India had 1,028.61 million internet subscribers on 31 December 2025, while higher-education enrolment reached 4.50 crore in 2023–24. The proposed AI–EE–SDG–VB 2047 Framework is based on curriculum integration, capacity building, data and innovation, community engagement, and ethics and governance. The paper argues that technological progress must be accompanied by ecological intelligence, social inclusion and accountable human judgement.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and First-Principles Physics for the Discovery of Sustainable Topological Heusler Materials: Prospects for Spintronics and Energy-Efficient Technologies in Viksit Bharat 2047
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), first-principles computational methods, and advanced functional materials provides new opportunities for the accelerated discovery of energy-efficient quantum and spintronic materials. Heusler alloys are particularly attractive because their chemical composition and structural ordering can be systematically modified to obtain desirable magnetic, electronic, topological, and thermoelectric properties. Magnetic Heusler compounds with strong spin–orbit coupling can exhibit Weyl points, band crossings, Berry-curvature hotspots, and enhanced anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC). Representative literature systems demonstrate the potential of this materials family: Co2MnGa has a reported calculated AHC of approximately −1310 Scm⁻¹, while Co2MnAl reaches approximately −1631 Scm⁻¹; Co2CrAl illustrates strong Fermi-level dependence, with its AHC increasing from approximately −313 Scm⁻¹ to about 1089 Scm⁻¹ after energy tuning. This work proposes an integrated density functional theory (DFT) and AI framework for the systematic discovery and optimization of sustainable topological Heusler materials. DFT calculations provide the physics-based evaluation of structural stability, magnetic ordering, electronic structure, spin–orbit coupling, Berry curvature, AHC, and ANC, while machine-learning models can learn composition–structure–property relationships and accelerate screening across unexplored chemical spaces. The proposed workflow includes stability screening, magnetic-ground-state analysis, electronic and topological characterization, Berry-curvature calculations, anomalous transverse transport calculations, machine-learning prediction, and independent DFT validation. Chemical substitution and carrier tuning are considered as strategies for positioning topological features near the Fermi level and enhancing transverse transport. Literature examples such as Pt2CrRh, with reported AHC of approximately 1966 Scm⁻¹ and ANC of approximately 7.50 Am⁻¹K⁻¹, and (Co0. 8Ni0.2)2FeSn, with reported AHC of approximately −2568 Scm⁻¹ and ANC of approximately 8.27 Am⁻¹K⁻¹, illustrate the potential of chemical tuning for achieving large transverse responses. The proposed DFT–AI strategy can therefore provide an efficient route toward identifying promising materials for spintronics, spin-caloritronics, low-power electronics, and thermal-energy conversion.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Higher Education Courses: A Maturity-Based Approach Using EMBED+
items.abstract: Digital transformation has become a strategic priority for higher education institutions (HEIs), with blended learning environments (BLEs) increasingly positioned as sustainable approaches that combine online and face-to-face learning. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering these environments, offering opportunities for personalised guidance, adaptive learning support, automated feedback, and enhanced media design. However, AI adoption often remains fragmented and technology-driven, creating challenges related to pedagogical coherence, ethics, equity, and sustainability. This paper argues that AI integration in blended courses should be understood as a maturity process rather than as a question of technology adoption alone. Using the European Maturity Model for Blended Education Plus (EMBED+) as an analytical framework, this study explores how AI-supported practices can evolve across maturity stages. The analysis focuses on two course-level dimensions where AI has particular relevance: Blended Learner Guidance and Use of Media and Tools. Through a conceptual mapping approach, AI applications are aligned with four maturity stages: ad hoc, deliberate, responsive, and embedded. Findings indicate that mature AI integration is characterised not by advanced technologies, but by intentional pedagogical design, evidence-informed improvement, and adaptive deployment. The proposed framework provides educators, instructional designers, and institutional leaders with a shared language to evaluate and strengthen AI-enhanced blended learning practices.

items.title: INTEGRATING GENERATIVE AI INTO HEURISTIC APPROACHES TO FOREIGN LANGUAGE EDUCATION
items.abstract: The article critically analyzes and scientifically substantiates the paradigm of integrating modern information and communication technologies (ICT) and artificial intelligence (AI) tools into the system of heuristic foreign language teaching in higher education. The author demonstrates that the synergy of digital tools and generative AI serves as a powerful intensifier of the educational process, ensuring deep individualization, differentiation of learning, enhancement of students’ intrinsic motivation, and the development of their cognitive and creative autonomy. The study synthesizes practical experience in utilizing the digital ecosystem of Sumy State Pedagogical University named after A.S. Makarenko in combination with video conferencing services (Google Meet, Zoom) and adaptive AI technologies to organize flexible online learning. Particular attention is paid to the effectiveness of these tools under crisis conditions (the COVID-19 pandemic and martial law) both for the routine automation of assessment and for modeling open-ended creative tasks of an exploratory nature. The paper presents original methodological developments, including the electronic manual «Communicative Culture of Medical Students in Use», integrated with modern digital resources. Specific examples demonstrate how the use of ICT and AI assistants enables students to complete a full heuristic cycle: from analytical information processing to the generation, self-correction, and defense of their own original educational product. The author summarizes the undeniable advantages of the updated innovative higher education space, which transforms traditional subject-subject relations into a format of interactive partnership: “teacher – student – artificial intelligence”.
